Summary Finding **H1** from the adversarial audit of the MCP brick host (#856, #858). The host claims "no record, no result", but in practice it failed open. With an unwritable audit directory (a full disk takes the same path), a real `github_blockers` call over stdio returned `isError:false`, the full result and an `auditId`, and no record existed anywhere. Cause: `FileBarrierAuditSink.WriteAsync` only enqueues and never throws, and `StructuredBarrierAuditLog` swallows every sink exception. So `BrickMcpToolContributor`'s "ran but its audit record could not be written" branch could not be reached in the shipped composition. The existing test for that branch used a throwing `IBarrierAuditLog` stub that production never builds. ## Changes - `IConfirmingBarrierAuditSink` (Ashlar.Runtime): `WriteConfirmedAsync` completes once the event is written and flushed, throws when it is not, and waits for room instead of dropping when the queue is full. - `FileBarrierAuditSink` implements it. Confirmed and unconfirmed writes share one queue and one writer, so file order is still queue order. A failed flush now discards the writer, so the lost line is not written ahead of the next event. A confirmed write after dispose throws. `WriteAsync` behaviour is unchanged: it never throws. - `AddAshlarMcpBricks` records through a new `ConfirmedBarrierAuditLog`, which uses confirmed writes and propagates sink failures. The contributor then withholds the output and returns a tool error. A refusal whose record fails now says "was refused", not "ran". - Host README: the "audit sink is best-effort" known limit is replaced by "No record, no result" (flushed to the OS, not `fsync`ed). - CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]`. Rebased onto master 36d46ca67. The earlier flaky-test commit was dropped because #866 fixed the same assertion on master. ## Testing - On master 36d46ca67, in the devtest container: - `scripts/test-in-container.sh --project src/Ashlar.Mcp.Server.Tests/... --framework net8.0`: 57/57. - `--filter FullyQualifiedName~FileBarrierAuditSink` (net10.0): 26/26. - New regression tests: - `With_the_File_sink_unable_to_write_a_call_withholds_its_result_and_says_it_is_unaudited` uses the real `AddBarrierAuditSinks` and `AddAshlarMcpBricks` composition. - `With_the_File_sink_the_record_is_on_disk_when_the_call_returns`. - Five `FileBarrierAuditSinkConfirmedWriteTests`. - Mutation checks (`scripts/mutation-check.sh`, before the rebase): - `mcp-audit-unconfirmed` (confirmed write replaced by `WriteAsync`): **KILLED** red=failed:2/12 green=passed:12/12. - `sink-confirms-failure` (`TrySetException` replaced by `TrySetResult`): **KILLED** red=failed:1/69 green=passed:69/69. - Live stdio probe (`docs/mcp-host-adversarial-audit.md` in the project store) reproduced the fail-open before the fix. ## ProdStyle [skip-prod-style]: `FileBarrierAuditSink` (under `src/Ashlar.Runtime/Barriers/`) is wired into the API host too. Its unconfirmed `WriteAsync` path, the one ProdStyle hosts use, is unchanged and still never throws. The new behaviour is reached only through `IConfirmingBarrierAuditSink`, which only `AddAshlarMcpBricks` uses, and the real composition test above covers it. Evidence: the `make test-prod-style` selection (`Category=ProdStyle&FullyQualifiedName!~ForgeEndpointsTests&FullyQualifiedName!~FrameworkVirtualProdDemosTests`, net8.0) passes 150/150 on this branch in the devtest container. Touches records/docs: `src/Ashlar.Mcp.Server.Host/README.md` (Known limits), `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/knowledge-graph.*` (regenerated). ## Checklist - [x] Not a versioned release — skip - [x] Documentation updated
